newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India mixed on political concerns.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India mixed on political concerns.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts ended mixed on Thursday as market sentiment remained tense amid political uncertainty, traders said.
They said volumes were relatively light and investors were seeking clarity on prospects for the safe passage of the 1997/8 budget through parliament despite the political crisis.
"The market is tentative. If the budget gets through it will climb, if not we will be going down," a trader said.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition government faces a confidence vote on April 11 following the withdrawal of support by the Congress Party on Sunday.
SBI and Reliance attracted early interest following gains in Bombay shares, but traders said support soon faded. SBI ended 20 cents down at $20/$21 and Reliance added 37 cents to $16.25/17.25.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.17 points, or 0.23 percent, down at 73.65 points, with the premium over the local market at 18.17 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index added 21.26 points to 3,559.65.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 1.61 points, or 0.99 percent, down at 60.16, a premium of 24.61 percent over the local market.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 2.78 points, or 2.28 percent, at 124.83, a discount of 5.70 percent.
